extracted.intended_audience: policymakers and managers in the U.S. Navy and federal agencies, contracting officers, public administration researchers, and analysts of privatization/OMB A-76 implementation
extracted.subtask_description: A master's thesis analyzing the U.S. Navy's implementation of OMB Circular A-76, examining post-award results of contracting out and identifying costs that are underestimated or omitted in pre-award cost comparisons. The work highlights operational, accounting, staffing, and policy issues affecting realized savings and contract performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy of pre-award cost estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: The accuracy of pre-award cost estimates used to estimate post-award program savings (concern that pre-award estimates may be inaccurate and thus overstate savings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study examines whether pre-award cost estimates correctly predict actual post-award costs and savings for contracted operations; inaccuracies here are a central area of controversy in A-76 implementations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion/accounting of post-award costs in cost comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification of costs that are either underestimated or not accounted for in the cost comparison process when contracting out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the cost comparison process fully captures all post-award expenses (hidden or omitted costs) so that projected savings are realistic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award guidance and policy
rubrics_metrics.description: The need for post-award guidance and policy to govern how contracted operations are managed after award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend development and dissemination of clear post-award policies to ensure consistent handling of issues that arise once services are contracted out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field-level claimant guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The need for increased claimant guidance at the field level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide targeted, practical guidance to activity-level personnel (claimants) to help them implement and manage contracts and understand post-award responsibilities and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate cost accounting system
rubrics_metrics.description: The absence of an adequate cost accounting system to track costs related to contracted-out operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish or improve cost accounting systems so post-award costs can be accurately recorded, monitored, and compared to pre-award estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award program controls
rubrics_metrics.description: The lack of post-award program controls to manage contracted operations effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement program controls (monitoring, oversight, performance measurement) to ensure contractors meet expectations and to detect cost deviations early.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract administration staffing
rubrics_metrics.description: The need for increased contract administration staffing to administer and oversee contracted services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess and staff contract administration functions adequately to handle increased workload and ensure proper contract oversight and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget flexibility at contracted activities
rubrics_metrics.description: A problem with budget flexibility at activities that have contracted out (constraints arising after contracting out that affect budgets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine how contracting out affects local budgeting and provide mechanisms or policies to preserve necessary flexibility for activities that transition to contractor-provided services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance definition and specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuing problems with performance definition (unclear or inadequate performance specifications in contracts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure clear, measurable, and enforceable performance definitions in contracts to reduce disputes, ensure quality, and allow meaningful post-award evaluation.
